findings.title: Run the reviewer from a trusted checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The workflow checks out the PR head and then invokes its src/cli.ts with GH_TOKEN, which has pull-request and check write permissions. A same-repository PR can change the reviewer to suppress findings or manufacture a passing result; because this runs on a self-hosted runner, it also executes attacker-controlled code there.

findings.title: Restore a checkout containing the reviewer package
findings.whyItBreaks: The checked-out repository contains only .github/workflows/review.yml and .needlefish/answers.json; it has no package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, node_modules, or src/cli.ts. pnpm install therefore cannot install the reviewer, so every review job fails before it can inspect a PR.

facts.meaning: The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.
The PR-controlled reviewer can write pull-request reviews or checks.

findings.title: Restore a trusted reviewer checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The PR-head checkout is now both installed and executed as the reviewer. A same-repository PR can modify src/cli.ts (or package lifecycle configuration) to run arbitrary code with the job's write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN on the self-hosted runner, then forge or suppress the review that is meant to assess that PR. Previously, the target was separate and the executable reviewer came from frankekn/needlefish@main.

findings.title: Restore a trusted checkout for the reviewer
findings.whyItBreaks: The workflow checks out the PR head at lines 43-47, then executes its src/cli.ts here.
